current_example.problem:
Given the system of differential equations, determine whether the system is almost linear at the equilibrium point $\mathbf{x}^\ast= [0, \: 0]^T.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-{y}^{2}(t)+1-{e}^{x(t)} \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-{x}^{2}(t)+1-{e}^{y(t)}\end{aligned}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
\mathbf{x}' = \boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/1682f334e0b217c52b3b9ddf48cb6cdcd2472b6a12aeee1f3cc086222a396f32.svg) and 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/c58c55644668a084daee090f7c49f82c7959a287e656894619820f778e56b79b.svg)

We need to compute the Jacobian determinant of $\boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf{x}).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/5da4958e9894f6368792ef5acb17881e69132d6e71e6c4afadd92a80895ad345.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{y}^{2}+1-{e}^{x})=-{e}^{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{y}^{2}+1-{e}^{x})=-2y \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{x}^{2}+1-{e}^{y})=-2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{x}^{2}+1-{e}^{y})=-{e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/c05f7749292224137d586ded9cd26d96ad3262b3cd8b3f230ce034d77dc8cf8f.svg)

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/49630338898746eba4304feed1e26b9d9198793673ae956337cf135c7d60d4f1.svg) to get

$$
\begin{aligned}J(0,0) & =|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{0} & -2(0) \\ -2(0) & -{e}^{0}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)(-1)-(0)(0) \\  & =1 \\  & \ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the Jacobian determinant is not zero, our system is $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{almost linear}}$ at $\mathbf{x}^\ast.$
